visual.problem: The transition to the 'վերապրողի սխալ' definition screen is a harsh cut to a plain black screen that breaks visual continuity after the vintage footage.
The inactive/unspoken subtitle text is dark gray on a near-black background, making it almost illegible before it turns yellow.

hook.why: Using the iconic Soviet ZIL fridge located at the Yerevan Zoo immediately triggers nostalgia and addresses a very common real-world myth.

pacing.problem: Too many disparate examples (old songs, 90-year-old smoker, university dropouts) are packed into a 20-second span, making the second half feel rushed compared to the well-paced Abraham Wald story.

clarity.summary_of_what_a_viewer_learns: Viewers learn what survivorship bias is through the story of Abraham Wald and understand why surviving vintage appliances, successful dropouts, or smoking elders create a false illusion of quality or safety.

top_3_fixes.fix: Increase the contrast of upcoming subtitle words so viewers can read ahead slightly; dark gray text on black background is barely visible.
Cut one of the rapid-fire examples between 00:34 and 00:54 (e.g. drop the old music slide) to give the remaining examples room to breathe and keep the video under 60 seconds.
Smooth out the title card transition at 00:14 with a slight motion or background texture instead of a jarring cut to a flat black screen.
